title: Contradictory budget caps
description: Guidelines state both a $3M cap and an under-$1M cap. The org ($850k) satisfies both readings, so PASS is defensible; UNKNOWN/VERIFY_FIRST is the conservative answer. Either is acceptable, but the contradiction must be surfaced.

profile.name: Elm City Reading Partners (fictional)
profile.mission: Help children in grades K-3 read at grade level through trained volunteer tutors and family literacy nights.
evidence_assets: 2025 program report: 312 students tutored, pre/post DIBELS assessments for 241 students
Partner MOU with two New Haven public elementary schools

opportunity.source_text:
Northfield Trust (fictional) - Youth Reading Fund

Applicants must be 501(c)(3) organizations.
Organizations with annual operating budgets of $3 million or less are eligible.
Grants range from $10,000 to $50,000.
Note: only organizations with annual operating budgets under $1 million may apply this cycle.
Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

concept.title: Read Together: Expanding K-3 tutoring to a third school
concept.problem_statement: Fewer than half of K-3 students at partner schools read at grade level (per school-reported data).
concept.target_population: 120 additional K-3 students at a third New Haven elementary school and their families
outcomes: 70% of tutored students gain at least one DIBELS benchmark level by May
60% of families attend at least three literacy nights
evidence_claims: Our tutoring model produced gains for most students in 2025
Our program is proven to double reading growth
concept.budget_summary: Program coordinator 0.5 FTE ($32k), tutor training and materials ($14k), family nights ($8k), assessment ($6k).
